key_insight: Better reliability diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening or reduce DFT verification costs at a required recall.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate reliability tools by the DFT they help avoid while retaining near-hull candidates, rather than by diagnostic accuracy alone.
method: Rank candidate crystals with MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3 before DFT verification.
Test novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits against a recall-constrained screening objective.
Use two oracle analyses to distinguish misaligned reliability targets from finite-budget audit limitations.
evidence_signal: Across all three interventions, improvements in their immediate diagnostic targets did not reliably translate into better downstream screening decisions.
watch_item: Audit-guided model routing depends on both decision-aligned targets and sufficient audit information; sparse audits did not yield robust benefits in the evaluated settings.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
